title: The Self-Photographing Debtscape

features.name: the self-measuring plot
features.desc-on-touch: Land that takes pictures of itself at dusk to prove how much it owes. Each photograph shows a different sunset, a different debt.

features.name: the accumulating frame
features.desc-on-touch: A structure made of stacked photographs. Each image carries the weight of unpaid ground. The stack grows heavier as you watch.

features.name: the lens that owes
features.desc-on-touch: A camera that photographs only debts. Every image it takes shows you what this place is obligated to remember.

features.name: the mirror-crop field
features.desc-on-touch: Fields that show themselves differently depending on who's looking. They photograph themselves as poor to richer neighbours, as rich to poorer ones.

features.name: the ledger in light
features.desc-on-touch: Shadows that keep count. Each shadow is a marker of something this land owes; they grow longer with every photograph.

inscription: a place that has learned to document its own obligation; every photograph it takes is another entry in the ledger it keeps against itself

file.name: Dusk_Photographs_Registry_Incomplete.jpg
file.note: Images of the same paddock at sunset, taken decades apart. The shadows in each photo have grown longer. In the newest one, the land casts a shadow it does not occupy.

reverie.title: REVERIE — the field photographed
narr: She stands at the edge of the paddock, camera
ready, waiting for the light to hit just right.
You know she's counting the shadows—measuring
what the land owes, what it remembers. She
shoots. The shutter sounds like a debt being
recorded. The ground itself becomes evidence.
